events.title: The Virgin of Guadalupe Appears to Juan Diego
events.description: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary first appeared to the indigenous Mexican convert Juan Diego on Tepeyac Hill, near present-day Mexico City.
events.significance: The apparition is the origin of the devotion to Our Lady of Guadalupe. She is now one of the most venerated religious figures in Latin America and a lasting symbol of Mexican identity.

events.title: Battle of Ayacucho
events.description: Patriot forces led by Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Spanish royalist army in the highlands of Peru.
events.significance: The victory effectively ended Spanish colonial rule in South America and secured the independence of Peru.

events.title: The Mother of All Demos
events.description: At a computer conference in San Francisco, engineer Douglas Engelbart gave a public demonstration of the computer mouse, hypertext and a graphical user interface. He also showed video conferencing and collaborative editing.
events.significance: The demo previewed much of modern personal computing decades before it became everyday technology.

events.title: Smallpox Eradication Is Certified
events.description: A global commission of scientists certified that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, after a long international vaccination campaign.
events.significance: Smallpox became the first human disease to be wiped out. It remains a landmark of global public health cooperation.
